A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDeC research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison. Relocated material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, a 20-participant user study, ablations, and additional empirical studies in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds prompt-order experiments, optimization diagnostics, backbone comparisons, and a lighting-shift evaluation.

M1.justification: The forward-and-backward eigenvalue optimization, absolute-excursion calculation, weighting, and embedding reconstruction in Equations 6–8 remain unchanged. Changing the backward-phase description from removing to recovering identity components corrects its explanation; the additional backbones use the existing procedure.

E1.justification: ConsiStory+, pose-conditioned generation, personalization, multiple-subject generation, and the existing Nano Banana scenarios are retained. Appendix J.4 adds a limited new scenario involving extreme illumination and colored lighting, illustrated with a bowl of bananas in Figure 20.

E2.justification: The main comparison methods remain unchanged. Supplementary comparisons add SD3 and Flux as baselines against their SDeC-equipped counterparts. Figure 20 also newly compares Nano Banana directly with SDXL+SDeC under lighting shifts.

E3.justification: The original benchmark size, metrics, and user-study design remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce reversed ID/scene prompt order and MMDiT backbones using weighting strength Omega=10, while retained UNet experiments use Omega=1. These are supplementary settings, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the diagnostic analyses with prompt-order sensitivity in Appendix H.3, eigenvalue trajectories during optimization in H.4, and an extreme-lighting failure case in J.4. The original component ablations, parameter sensitivity, and contextualization visualizations remain; moving the qualitative ablation into Section 5.2 adds no new analysis itself.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The parenthetical differences in v2 Table 5 represent changes caused by prompt reversal, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. New Tables 5–6 substantially expand reported results through prompt-order scores and quantitative backbone comparisons. For example, v2 reports DreamSim-F of 0.2875 for SD3 and 0.2644 for SD3+SDeC within the new comparison. Added figures report optimization behavior, SD3/Flux examples, and lighting-direction failures for both tested systems.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, Corollaries 1–2, and their proofs in Appendices A–D retain the same assumptions, bounds, and reasoning. Equation reformatting and added discussion of trade-offs and standard computational costs do not introduce a new formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain scene contextualization as a source of identity shift, theoretical characterization, and training-free per-scene embedding editing that balances identity preservation and scene diversity. Adding SD3 and Flux examples supports the existing generality claim without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through explanations of prompt-order sensitivity, scene-dependent eigenvalue behavior, and scalability prospects. It explicitly discusses the disentanglement–coherence trade-off and identifies extreme lighting as an applicability limitation. The earlier limitations concerning idealized subspaces and indirect contextualization control are retained.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code and data availability; v2 supplies a project repository URL instead. v2 also adds SD3/Flux checkpoint references and architecture-dependent parameter guidance in Appendices E.1 and H.2. Existing hardware and baseline implementation information remain unchanged; repository accessibility is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Esser et al., Ronneberger et al., Halko et al., and Williams and Seeger for generative architectures and possible scalable approximations. The related-work taxonomy and principal positioning against existing consistent-generation methods remain intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the overall section sequence are retained. v2 corrects wording, expands explanations, moves qualitative ablation discussion into Section 5.2, reorganizes the later appendices, and updates affiliation, conference-header, and acknowledgment text.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–6 and Figures 11, 15, and 20. It also moves the existing qualitative ablation figure into the main text and splits v1 Figure 12 into enlarged Figures 8–9. These substantially extend and reorganize the visual presentation; the corresponding retained image results are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone comparisons strengthen evidence for generality, while prompt-order diagnostics and the lighting failure case clarify behavior and practical limits. Parameter guidance, the project link, and the corrected backward-phase explanation improve usability. These are useful incremental gains over an already substantial evaluation; the central method, proofs, and main results remain unchanged.
